questions.q: What is the real difference between running dbt run then dbt test as two commands, versus running dbt build?
options: dbt run then dbt test builds every model first regardless of test outcomes, while dbt build interleaves tests into dependency order, stopping before building on top of a failure
dbt build only runs tests, never models
There is no real difference; they always produce identical results
dbt run is the newer, recommended command and dbt build is deprecated
questions.explain: dbt build's dependency-ordered interleaving is what actually stops bad data from propagating downstream within the same run.

questions.q: In the walkthrough where orders.amount fails its non_negative test, what happens to customers that same run?
options: customers builds but with the row removed automatically
customers builds normally since it doesn't reference amount directly
customers never gets built that run, because dbt build stops the branch of the dependency graph downstream of the failed test
The entire Snowflake database is locked until the issue is fixed
questions.explain: Because customers depends on orders via ref(), dbt build halts that downstream branch rather than building a mart on top of data that just failed a real test.

questions.q: Why does this platform use the default severity: error for non_negative rather than severity: warn?
options: A negative payment amount reaching customers.lifetime_value and then Power BI is a worse outcome than stopping the build and asking a human to look at it
error severity runs tests faster than warn severity
severity: warn is not valid dbt syntax
warn severity requires a separate paid dbt feature
questions.explain: severity: warn only logs a note while still letting bad data flow downstream — for a money-column rule like this, blocking is the deliberate choice.

questions.q: What does this lesson's gate become once it's wired into Chapter 6's CI/CD pipeline?
options: A redundant check that duplicates what a developer already confirmed locally
Something that only applies to the Power BI layer, not to dbt models
A manual step a reviewer has to remember to run themselves
A real governance control, since it now runs automatically on every proposed change before that change can merge, with no developer action required to trigger it
questions.explain: A safety net that only runs when a developer remembers to run it isn't a governance control — automatic enforcement on every PR is what makes it one.

questions.q: What does "blocking the branch" mean in the context of a dbt build test failure?
options: Every model downstream of the failed model, via ref(), does not get built in that run
dbt automatically creates a new git branch to isolate the failure
The entire git branch is deleted automatically
Only the exact column that failed is removed from the output table
questions.explain: Blocking the branch refers to the dependency graph: nothing downstream of a failed test's model gets built in that same dbt build run.
